 ORDER
Since pleadings are complete, therefore, looking to the dispute involved in the case, it is heard finally.

2. The petitioner by the instant petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has claimed the following relief (s):-
"7.1

To constitute a Special Investigation Team or order for High Power Special Agency to investigate into the manipulation and concealment of evidence to claim compensation u/s 140/166 of MV Act and 357(3) of CrPC.

7.2 For commanding the respondent no.1 & 2 to take all possible departmental action against respondent no.3 4 & 5.
7.3 To suitably prosecute respondent no.3,4 & 5.
7.4 To pass any other order deem fit in the facts of the case."

3. The petitioner by filing the instant petition has tried to establish that a false case of accident got registered against him mentioning therein that he with his car had not only dashed the motorcycles of the complainants, but also caused injuries to them whereas according to him, no such incident took place as his car was parked at the corner of the road and in fact, the riders of the motorcycles riding their motorcycles rashly and negligently collided with his car and sustained injuries.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that a completely false case got registered against the petitioner as the incident which happened because of rash and negligent riding of motorcycles but had been projected as if it was the petitioner who dashed both the motorcycles by his car.

sentences.text:
He submits that although at the time of incident, the vehicle of the petitioner was parked at the corner of the road, but it has been shown that the driver of the car (present petitioner) driving it rashly and negligently hit the motorcycles of the injured and caused injuries to them.
5.
On the other hand, learned Government Advocate has opposed the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner and relied upon the reply filed by them.

He has submitted that from the material collected by the police during investigation, it will be clear that nothing wrong has been committed by the police while registering a case against the petitioner.

6. Considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties, perusal of record and after examining the material produced by the counsel for the petitioner through PEN drive, this Court is of the opinion that in a petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, it is not proper to probe an independent or parallel enquiry to ascertain whether the stand of the petitioner is correct or of the case projected by the police.

Prima facie, this Court is of the opinion that when the police is investigating the matter in which car and motorcycles both were involved, then it would not be proper to handover the investigation to some other independent agency.

However, expecting a fair investigation, since instructions have already been issued to the police authorities so that charge-sheet can be submitted before the Court expeditiously, therefore, it is not proper for this Court to enter into the said arena and hand over the investigation to some other agency.
7. Consequently, the petition being devoid of merits, stands dismissed.
(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE Devashish DEVASHISH MISHRA 2023.10.20 10:48:55 +05'30'
